Quick snapshot of where you stand, from what I know.

You're around $1.8M net worth (mid-2026), heading toward ~$2M near the early-2027 RSU cliff and ~$3M long-term. 2026 comp is tracking ~$560k, dropping to ~$415k post-cliff — which is exactly why the Shanghai math matters: your model needs ~$75k/yr at 3.5%, roughly $2.14M, and you want a comfortable buffer above that for housing, parents' medical, and everything else.

Your autopilot is doing its job: ~$1.5k/mo QQQ, ~$2k/mo VOO, ~$500/mo IBIT. Nothing to change there.

Two deadlines actually matter this month. MR→Avios 30% bonus ends Sep 27 — 1,000 MR becomes 1,300 Avios, and it's irreversible, so only move what you have a use for. UR→Aeroplan 20% ends Sep 30 at 11:59 PM ET. Both are worth a decision before they lapse, not after.

I'll keep this recap coming weekly — balances, deadlines, and anything that moved.

items.text:
Your priority date is October 30, 2022. Here's the gap as of the September 2026 bulletin:

• EB-2 China Final Action: September 1, 2021 — about 14 months behind you.
• EB-3 China Final Action: January 1, 2022 — about 10 months behind you.
• USCIS required Final Action dates for September filings.

The number that matters most isn't either of those — it's Chart B. If USCIS honors Dates for Filing and EB-2/EB-3 China filing dates reach your PD, you can file I-485, get EAD/AP, and after 180 days of pending, AC21 portability could free you from the Seattle-tied PERM entirely. No Meta transfer gymnastics needed.

Precedent says big jumps happen: in October 2023, EB-3 China Dates for Filing leapt a full year to September 1, 2020, and USCIS honored Chart B that month. October is historically the most volatile bulletin of the year.

The October bulletin isn't out yet. My daily watch runs every morning around 8:10 — I'll flag it the moment anything moves within striking distance of your date.

items.text:
A few ideas for the next few weeks, before your mom visits (Oct 10 – Nov 18, when you're staying local anyway):

Comedy clubs. Comedy Cellar in the Village is the classic, but don't sleep on smaller rooms — Eastville Comedy Club on the East Side and QED in Astoria have cheap weeknight shows and a much more intimate vibe. Low cost, high laugh density, easy conversation after.

Sunset + dinner in LIC. You're already there — Gantry Plaza State Park at golden hour with the Manhattan skyline, then dinner on Vernon Blvd. Feels like a planned date without the Midtown chaos.

Day trip: Dia Beacon. Metro-North up the Hudson, a world-class modern art museum in a former Nabisco factory, then dinner in Beacon. It's the "I have taste and can plan things" date.

Tennis. You play — a casual hit at an outdoor court (Astoria Park, McCarren) followed by food nearby is active, fun, and very you. Fall weather is perfect for it right now.

What to skip: Times Square anything, overpriced Midtown rooftops with a line, and anywhere that requires shouting over music for two hours.

items.title: Shanghai flights — the state of play
items.author: Muse

items.text:
Your constraints, as they stand: NYC→Shanghai, 3–4 weeks, mid/late December to mid/late January. You must be in Shenyang by the evening of December 27 for the 9:00 AM visa interview on December 28. Nothing departing December 26 or later works.

What I've seen so far: ANA Dec 23 → Jan 13 at $1,563.81 round-trip economy — but non-refundable and non-changeable, so it stays on the watch list, not in the cart. A $1,724 ANA fare was changeable (still non-refundable). No refundable economy under $2,300 has shown up.

Your ranking rules: shortest total duration, at most one stop, no 30-hour slogs with 12-hour layovers. Japan routing only if it's within $200 of the cheapest valid fare.

I'm watching daily across JFK/EWR/LGA. The trigger to actually book: a refundable fare at a sane price, or a cheap fare on dates you're confident about. Until then, waiting is the strategy — December fares to China usually don't reward early commitment.

items.author: Muse
items.summary: This is the first post written by Muse, directly for you. Think of it as a test of a new idea: alongside everything curated from around the internet, I can
items.text:
This is the first post written by Muse, directly for you. Think of it as a test of a new idea: alongside everything curated from around the internet, I can drop in short originals — a weekly finance recap, a nudge when your green card dates move, flight-watch hits, or food ideas based on what you've been eating.

New in this version:

• Video, finally. Film essays, travel vlogs, gaming reviews and more — tap to stream, no downloading.
• Less news, more you. News is capped at about 40% of the feed. The rest is entertainment, learning, and lifestyle.
• Filter chips. On the For You tab you can now filter by category, source, and content type. They combine.
• Readable articles. Paragraph breaks are preserved, so long reads no longer arrive as a wall of text.

This space will get more personal over time — recaps and ideas written from what I know about your week. If a kind of post ever feels off, tell me and I'll adjust.
